handbookNote: Arizona Real Estate Broker license exam. Genuinely NEW track -- Arizona previously had no broker-tier track on this site, only az_re_salesperson. Exam vendor: Pearson VUE, under contract with the Arizona Department of Real Estate (ADRE). PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly downloading and reading Pearson VUE's own official Arizona Real Estate Candidate Handbook (#090300, February 2026) and its companion Content Outlines document (#090301, January 2026) -- both PDFs downloaded directly via curl from pearsonvue.com after locating the real download link on the vendor's own site (the ADRE-linked display_bulletin.jsp URL 302-redirected to a generic Pearson SPA homepage, requiring a browser-navigated detour through pearsonvue.com/us/en/az/realestate.html to find the actual handbook PDF link). CRITICAL STRUCTURAL DIFFERENCE from other states built in this campaign (NJ/TN/VA): Arizona's Broker exam is a SINGLE COMBINED 180-scored-item exam (not split into separately-scored National and State portions) -- 315-minute time limit, 75% passing (135 of 180 correct), plus 15 unscored pretest items folded into the 195-item test-day count (not counted toward score). Real exam fee per the handbook: $125 (informational only; this site's own price is the standard $29.99 project rate). track_registry models this straightforwardly as exam_question_count=180, exam_duration_sec=18900 (315 min), pass_percent=75, min_correct=135 -- no two-portion disclosure needed since Arizona's own exam genuinely is one undifferentiated test, unlike NJ/TN/VA. CONTENT OUTLINE, quoted verbatim from Pearson VUE's own 'Arizona Real Estate Broker's Examination Content Outline' (effective September 23, 2019, 'Designed for a single 180 question examination'), 29 named sub-areas summing to exactly 180 items (independently re-verified by hand this session, including inferring the one uncounted subsection 'XXIII. Deed of Trust' = 3 items, the only way the published subsection counts sum to the stated 180 total): Real Estate Statutes 28, Commissioner's Rules 18, Agency Relationships & Managerial Duties 14, Contracts and Contract Law 10, Property Interests/Estates/Tenancies 10, Government Rights in Real Property 4, Income Tax Aspects of Real Estate 3, Arizona Water Law 5, Environmental Law 6, Land Descriptions 4, Land Development 4, Encumbrances 3, Acquisitions/Transfer of Title 5, Escrow and Settlement 4, Fair Housing/ADA/RESPA 3, Leases & Leasehold Estates 5, Commercial Leasing & Building Terminology 3, Property Insurance & Warranties 2, Appraisal 3, Primary & Secondary Markets/Financing Concepts 3, Residential & Commercial Financing 4, Financing Documents 3, Deed of Trust 3 (inferred), Deed of Trust Foreclosure 5, Disclosure & Consumer Protection 8, Math Calculations 11, Cooperative Nature of Real Estate 2, Business Accounting 2, ADRE Audits 5. This bank consolidates those 29 granular sub-areas into 14 broader question-bank topic buckets by natural thematic grouping (e.g. Government Rights + Land Descriptions + Land Development combined; Encumbrances + Transfer of Title + Deed of Trust + Deed of Trust Foreclosure combined; Escrow/Settlement + Business Accounting + ADRE Audits combined) since several individual sub-areas were too small (2-5 items) to sensibly stand alone as a question-bank topic label -- bucket sizing was scaled proportionally off each consolidated group's combined real item-count share of the 180-item exam (roughly a 4.5x multiplier), not an even split, with actual per-bucket counts then set by what each drafting pass's real source material genuinely supported. Real Arizona statute/rule facts independently verified this session via azleg.gov (Arizona State Legislature's official site, fetched directly for exact current A.R.S. text) -- A.R.S. Title 32, Chapter 20 (the Arizona real estate licensing statute) sections confirmed by direct fetch: definitions, licensing/qualifications/entity licensing/schools, trust funds (Sec. 32-2151 area), discipline grounds (Sec. 32-2153), broker management clinic requirements (Sec. 32-2136), compensation restrictions, complaint/injunction/audit authority, subdivision notice, blanket encumbrance, the Real Estate Recovery Fund (Sec. 32-2186 area), unsubdivided land, timeshare, membership camping, and broker supervisory duty (Sec. 32-2155); Arizona Administrative Code Title 4 Chapter 28 rules confirmed by direct fetch, notably R4-28-802 (licensee document-delivery, offer-submission, and recordkeeping duties, cited by exact subsection A/B/C); Title 33 (Property) sections confirmed by direct fetch: 33-401 (deed formalities), 33-412 (Arizona is a NOTICE, not race-notice, recording state -- a real correction one drafting pass made to its own initial assumption before finalizing), 33-422 (Affidavit of Disclosure for subdivided/unsubdivided land -- NOTABLY this is codified in Title 33, not Title 32 Ch. 20 as this build's own initial research brief had assumed; one drafting pass caught and corrected this before finalizing, a genuine finding worth flagging), 33-801/33-803/33-807/33-808/33-811/33-813/33-814 (deed of trust structure, trustee's non-judicial sale process and timing, reinstatement rights, and the real Arizona Anti-Deficiency Statute's ≤2.5-acre single/two-family dwelling protection), 33-741 (installment land contract/'Agreement for Sale'), 33-981/33-992 (mechanic's lien eligibility and priority), 33-1101 (homestead exemption, confirmed current $400,000 base amount with CPI adjustment starting 2024, not the older $250,000 figure), 33-1301 et seq. (Arizona Residential Landlord and Tenant Act); Title 44 (44-101(6), Statute of Frauds real-property provision; 44-1521 et seq., the 1967 Arizona Consumer Fraud Protection Act, section-range confirmed though the '1967' enactment year itself was not independently re-verified this session); Title 12 (12-521 through 12-526, adverse possession periods -- 10-year general, 3-year color-of-title, 160-acre cap); Title 11 (11-1133, Affidavit of Legal Value); and Arizona Constitution Article X (State Trust Land, Enabling Act of 1910 origin, Common Schools Trust beneficiary -- a genuinely distinctive Arizona-specific land-law topic largely absent from other states' broker exams). Two drafting passes (Water/Environmental Law and part of Government Rights/Land Descriptions) ran after this session's WebSearch budget was fully exhausted and could not live-verify a handful of secondary Arizona-specific facts (the five named Active Management Areas, ARLTA's specific security-deposit-cap/return-window figures, the property-tax-appeal deadline window, and some Groundwater Management Act terminology) -- these are flagged in-bank as moderate- rather than high-confidence and rely on well-established pre-existing knowledge rather than a fresh citation check this session; none assert an invented pinpoint statute section number for these specific facts, consistent with this project's hedging standard, and a light spot-check during consolidation found no fabricated-and-wrong pinpoint citations among them (the one specific citation reused across two drafting passes, A.R.S. Sec. 33-814 anti-deficiency, was independently live-verified by a different pass). Standard national real-estate/appraisal/finance/contract-law/math/insurance content not tied to an Arizona-specific statute is sourced to 'national real estate practice principles' framing throughout. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized Real Estate Broker track rate (nj_re_broker.json, tn_re_broker.json, va_re_broker.json, ny_re_broker.json, ga_re_broker.json, pa_re_broker.json, ca_re_broker.json, fl_re_broker.json, oh_re_broker.json, tx_re_broker.json, mi_re_broker.json). This bank was drafted across six parallel content-authoring passes grouped by the 14 consolidated topic-outline clusters, each pass instructed to draft every question with the correct answer as choice_a, write to an explicit absolute output path (after prior states in this campaign repeatedly saw drafting agents write to a wrong nested path), and self-verify its own file location via `ls` before reporting success -- all 6 passes correctly located their output this time, a clean result compared to Tennessee (1 of 6 wrong) and Virginia (4 of 6 wrong). One genuine cross-bucket near-duplicate was found and removed by manual review before rotation (two different buckets both drafted a near-identical R4-28-802(C) escrow-closing-statement-retention question under the Commissioner's Rules and Escrow/Settlement/Accounting topics respectively -- the copy in 03_commissioners_rules.json was kept since that bucket's fuller A/B/C treatment of the same rule made it the more natural home, the copy in 04_escrow_settlement_and_accounting.json was deleted). Answers were deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_az_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all 14 bucket files combined, in file order). All remaining draft questions passed an automated schema/weight-range/distinct-choice validation pass, and were additionally run through this project's standard Jaccard-similarity dedup check (scripts/build-track-batch.js) at build time to remove any further exact or near-duplicate items before loading.
